_comment: The actor registry: every identity that may act on eqdmc repositories, and the ceiling of what it may do. THIS IS THE SSOT. config/authorized-actors.yml is generated from it, and infra's broker identity policy derives from it -- do not hand-edit either. See ADR-0024/0026 (one App per role), ADR-0018 (broker request contract), ADR-0029 (scope every request to one repo).
_ceiling_vs_request: An App's permissions are the CEILING -- the blast radius of a stolen key. A broker request may ask for LESS: {"repo": "eqdmc/x", "permissions": {"contents": "write"}} mints a token with no issues or pull_requests rights. So a NEW APP is warranted only for a new CEILING that defends a control; a lower need is a scoped request and needs no App at all. This is why there is no push-bot (see #630).
_reachability: human_only = only a human at the host; host = the Unix socket (a human or a host process); network = mintable from a krun VM over the network. bin/security-invariants asserts the privileged ones; nothing holding workflows write may be network-reachable.
_status: active = the App exists and is installed; planned = intended but NOT created, so it may not be an authorized actor.

eqdmc-admin.note: Primary admin. Acts through Rax and the hardware signer; holds the YubiKey.

eqdmc-admin-bot.defends: Org config-as-code: rulesets, labels, repo settings, runner groups.
eqdmc-admin-bot.note: The only identity that may change org configuration. Replaces the ORG_CONFIG_TOKEN fine-grained PAT (#626). `human_only` is enforced by the `admin-apply` environment: the reconciler that mints it waits for @eqdmc-admin (#739). Without a reviewer there, the reachability is aspirational.

eqdmc-agent-bot.defends: The authoring identity. It can push branches and open PRs, but it cannot merge, cannot edit workflows, and cannot administrate. checks:read is a read of public check results that defends no control -- it is what lets the identity that is told to run `gh pr checks` actually run it (#687).
eqdmc-agent-bot.note: Installed org-wide. Its ceiling is deliberately short of merge, workflows and administration. checks:read needs the App grant in the org's App settings (#687); until that lands the registry is ahead of the live installation, and generate-identities.py --verify reports the drift.

eqdmc-merge-bot.defends: The only identity that may bypass branch protection to merge or tag.
eqdmc-merge-bot.note: Must never be network-reachable -- an agent that could reach it could merge around every gate. Asserted in bin/security-invariants.

eqdmc-build-bot.defends: Read-only CI and runner state. actions:write was never needed -- runner-ops.yml uses only read, and a dispatch can reach a job's secrets, so the write was a control it did not have to hold (#631). checks:read is what lets an agent see why a PR is blocked (#687).
eqdmc-build-bot.note: Reduced to actions:read + checks:read (#631). It no longer authors a PR: it lacks contents:write and pull_requests:write, so the allowlist entry was dead. Serves the `ops` profile.

eqdmc-session-bot.defends: The identity of the session-orchestrator webhook receiver (docker/session-orchestrator/server.py): it verifies GitHub deliveries, parses typed-issue metadata and routes to rax, agent or deploy. issues:write (comment) + checks:write (publish a check run) is the minimum for that job.
eqdmc-session-bot.note: NAMED CONSUMER: the session-orchestrator, deployed by bin/session-orch-deploy (`*Session-orchestrator via eqdmc-session-bot*`). #632's premise -- 'no webhook receiver exists' -- was false: the service, its WEBHOOK_SECRET and its compose file all exist. Do NOT retire the App while that consumer references it; confirm the orchestrator is live before pruning EITHER. It does not author a PR -- it holds no contents:write/pull_requests:write -- so `authors_prs: false` drops a dead allowlist entry.

eqdmc-ci-bot.defends: Workflow edits. workflows:write is the one permission that can rewrite a workflow to print a secret, so it is host-only. It also holds pull_requests:write so it can open the PR for the change it pushed -- without that, no bot can author a workflow PR, the human authors it, the human becomes the required CODEOWNER reviewer, and every such merge needs --admin, which bypasses every required check.
eqdmc-ci-bot.note: Host-only and un-bypassing. Adding pull_requests:write does not widen the blast radius an agent can reach: the network gate still cannot select it.

_decisions._comment: Non-App decisions that shape the set, recorded here so the rule survives the issue that produced it.
_decisions.eqdmc-push-bot: REJECTED, never created (#630): contents:write is a strict subset of agent-bot's ceiling and the broker already mints it as a scoped request -- {"repo": ..., "permissions": {"contents": "write"}}. A lower ceiling is a request, not an App.
_decisions.eqdmc-bootstrap-bot: REJECTED, never created (#1569): app_id 0. contents:write is a strict subset of agent-bot's ceiling and the broker mints it as a scoped request (ADR-0029); bootstrap is a time-bounded PROFILE lease (bin/eqdmc-bootstrap-auth, infra#1624), not an App. The dead token request was removed with the identity.

_authoring_note: authors_prs is AUTHORISATION (a policy choice). Capability is derivable: an App can only open a PR with contents:write AND pull_requests:write. The generator reports authorised-but-incapable apps rather than silently dropping them -- a permissions table taken from prose notes is not ground truth until it is verified against GitHub's installation API. A third permission matters for authoring: pull_requests:write. An App without it cannot open the PR for the branch it pushed, which is how the rax ended up using the human's credentials and the required CODEOWNERS review became unsatisfiable (#646).
_namespace: One namespace, derived not decorated. An App's key is `N-eqdmc-<name>.pem.age` where N is its tier; its login is `eqdmc-<name>-bot`; its profile is `<name>`. Secrets are `EQDMC_*`, labels `<prefix>:<value>`, workflows `<concern>.yml`. The registry is where a rename would have to happen, and the generator checks the key/tier agreement, so the namespace cannot drift in one file only.
_profiles: A profile is a broker REQUEST, not an App. The broker mints a token scoped to it, so a role that needs less than its App's ceiling needs no new App (see #630). Two invariants: a profile may never exceed its App's ceiling, and no agent-callable profile may select an App that bypasses branch protection -- an agent asks for a merge (auto-merge), and the merge queue performs it.

build.purpose: Implement one issue: branch, commits, open a PR, comment on the issue.

review.purpose: Review a PR: read the diff, comment, approve or request changes.

triage.purpose: Labels, comments, close or reopen issues.

merge.purpose: Ask for a merge. This profile deliberately does NOT hold merge-bot: it enables auto-merge and lets the merge queue do the merge, so no workspace ever holds ruleset bypass. contents:write is required to ARM auto-merge (enablePullRequestAutoMerge is refused with contents:read) -- without it the orchestrator role cannot ask for a merge at all.

ops.purpose: Read runner and check state (runner-ops). Read-only until #631 decides whether actions:write is ever needed.

workflows.purpose: Author a workflow change end to end on the host: push the branch and open the PR. The human then APPROVES -- a genuine second party -- instead of overriding with --admin. This is the only profile that may hold workflows:write, it is host-only, and it holds no ruleset bypass.

_roles: The org's SESSION roles (infra/config/agent-taxonomy.json: founder, bootstrap, recovery, build, research, advisor, review, orchestrator) mapped to a GitHub profile. One fact, one owner: the role taxonomy is infra's, the GitHub ceiling is this file's, and this map is the seam between them -- checked by bin/check-taxonomy (T1), so it cannot silently diverge. bin/identity-request resolves role -> profile -> broker request + git identity for a krun entrypoint or the orchestrator.

build.note: implement one issue: branch, commits, PR

review.note: read the diff, comment, approve or request changes

orchestrator.note: coordinate; asks for merges, never bypasses

bootstrap.note: the elevated HOST session: the only role that may edit a workflow
